newsitem.title: USA: Calif. teen arrested on suspicion of murdering mother.
newsitem.headline: Calif. teen arrested on suspicion of murdering mother.

text.p: Police said on Tuesday they had arrested a northern California teenager on suspicion of strangling his mother and dumping her body in a water-filled quarry.

Police in Rocklin, near Sacramento, said they had received reports that the 17-year-old boy had held parties at his house since his mother, 40-year-old Barbara Schultz, was murdered just over a week ago.
Rocklin police did not release the name of the boy because of his age.
The teenager was arrested on suspicion of murder on Monday, two days after his mother's body was found partially submerged at a quarry in Rocklin, police said.

Three of the boy's friends, one aged 17 and two aged 18, were also arrested on suspicion of helping the boy dispose of the body, police spokeswoman Kris Whitty said. They could be charged with being "accessories after the fact," she said.
"He (the son) and his mother were involved in a confrontation at which time he apparently strangled her," she said. It was not clear what started the argument.
Early the next morning the boy and his friends allegedly disposed of the body at the quarry, she said.
Whitty said police believed the boy returned to the quarry some time afterward and saw his mother's body had resurfaced, so he weighted the body to sink it.
